raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

Fixes #47501.

#45917 made `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8` turn a lazy (`BYPASSED`) TopK output into explicit `topk_ids`/`topk_weights` whenever it carries `num_token_non_padded`. That bound does not mean the batch has padded rows. `enable_num_token_non_padded()` attaches it to every forward whenever `moe_ep_size > 1`, in eager prefill and in every decode CUDA graph, padded or not. With `--ep > 1`, every block-FP8 MoE layer therefore left FlashInfer's fused in-kernel router and paid two extra launches per decode step:

| Per decode step, bs=1, TP rank 0 (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, 48 MoE layers, GB200) | parent of #45917 | #45917 | #45917 + this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPU kernels | 1562.7 | 1658.7 | 1562.7 |
| `_router_triton_kernel` (materialized softmax top-10 over 512 experts) | 0 | 48 x ~6.5 us | 0 |
| `mask_topk_ids_padded_region` | 0 | 48 x ~1.4 us | 0 |

Only the expert-placement remap (`expert_location_dispatch_info`) needs materialized routes: the in-kernel router cannot apply a logical-to-physical expert map, and before #45917 that case raised. A padding bound alone does not need them:

- With the standard dispatcher, padded rows never leave the rank.
- FlashInfer sizes its workspace from `num_tokens * top_k`.
- The caller drops padded-row outputs.

The same FP8 runner already routes padded rows in-kernel at EP=1, where the bound is `None`, and so do the FP4, BF16, and MXFP4 TRT-LLM runners. Masking does not pay for itself on padded batches either: con3 (decode bs 3, padded to the bs-4 graph) is faster without it (below).

## Modifications

- `BypassedTopKOutput.needs_select_experts` (`topk.py`): true when routing straight from logits would skip work that `select_experts` does:
  - the expert-placement remap;
  - routed-expert capture (`--enable-return-routed-experts`, unless the TopK opted out, as drafts do);
  - expert-distribution recording (`expert_distribution_recorder_mode` set);
  - routing simulation (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_UNIFORM_EXPERTS` / `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ROUND_ROBIN_EXPERTS`).
  This is the same set that `mimo_v2` already uses to gate its bypassed TopK.
- `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8`: materialize a bypassed TopK only when `needs_select_experts`. A padding bound alone keeps the in-kernel router. The predicate does not depend on the bound, so the unbounded (EP=1) FP8 path now also runs these hooks.
- `FusedMoE.forward` under tc-piecewise CUDA graphs uses the same predicate to keep such outputs off the opaque logits-only op. That op rebuilds a partial `TopKConfig`, which `select_experts` must not run from.
- The rest of #45917 is unchanged:
  - remap support on the bypassed path
  - materialized/routed inputs and FP16 score promotion
  - deferred finalize on materialized routes
  - CUTLASS/W4A8 route producers
- The `layer.py` tc-piecewise check still forwards bounded lazy outputs through `forward_impl`, because consumers that do materialize (the CUTLASS runner, the FlashInfer A2A dispatcher) still need the bound there.
- Tests:
  - `test_fp8_padding_bound_still_runs_select_experts_hooks` (CPU): a padding bound with no placement remap, run with capture, recording, and simulation each enabled in turn. The runner must reach the routed kernel, and the hook must see the real-row IDs.
  - `test_piecewise_lazy_routing_with_capture_keeps_the_full_config` (CPU): an unbounded lazy output with capture enabled under tc-piecewise must go through `forward_impl`, not the opaque op.
  - Both fail on the previous head of this PR (4 failures) and pass now.
  - `test_topk_routing_inputs.py` (CPU): a bounded `BYPASSED` output without a placement remap must reach the logits (in-kernel) kernel, and padded-row outputs are left to the caller. With a placement remap it must still reach the routed kernel with padded IDs `-1` and zeroed rows. The deferred-finalize ABI check follows the same split. On the unfixed runner these assertions fail (25 subtests); with this PR they pass.
  - `test_flashinfer_fp8_routed.py` (Blackwell GPU): bounded routes are materialized in the test before reaching the runner. It still covers valid/partial/inactive/recovery CUDA-graph replay, poisoned padded rows, and deferred finalize on the materialized path.

## Accuracy Tests

This change only selects which existing FlashInfer entry point runs. For padding-only bounds, it restores the in-kernel routing used before #45917 and still used at EP=1, so the expert selection and weights for real rows are unchanged.

Routed-expert capture, end to end. `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, TP4/EP4, `--enable-return-routed-experts`, `/generate` with `return_routed_experts: true`, temperature 0, 24 new tokens. That gives 34 tokens x 48 layers x top-10 = 16,320 IDs.

| SGLang source | Returned IDs | Rows with 10 distinct IDs | Experts seen | SHA-1 of IDs |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `main` `5008726431` | valid, 0..511 | 100% | 512 | `acb9b308836d894e` |
| this PR without the capture fix | all zeros | 0% | 1 | `ae4081ce70ff5cf0` |
| this PR | valid, 0..511 | 100% | 512 | `acb9b308836d894e` (same as `main`) |

The generated text is identical across all three.

On 1x GB200 in `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`:

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| this PR | 78 passed, 174 subtests passed |
| `main` | 78 passed, 174 subtests passed |
| new tests on the unfixed runner | 25 subtests fail |

The test files were `test_topk_routing_inputs.py`, `test_native_moe_routing_policy.py`, `test_fp8_moe_runner_ownership.py`, `test_standard_dispatcher.py`, `test_standard_dispatcher_runner_backend.py`, and `test_flashinfer_fp8_routed.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup:
- Model and launch: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` on 1x GB200 node, `--tp 4 --ep 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.79 --context-length 9216`, `SGLANG_RADIX_FORCE_MISS=1`.
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` (torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2).
- Load: AIPerf 0.12.0, completions, streaming, ISL 8000 / OSL 1000, 5 x concurrency requests after 8 warmups, 3 trials each. All rows ran on the same node.

| SGLang source | con1 trials (tok/s) | con1 mean | con1 ITL | con3 trials (tok/s) | con3 mean |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| `8b9b992e41` (parent of #45917) | 227.7 / 228.2 / 228.0 | 228.0 | 4.22 ms | 556.0 / 558.6 / 556.1 | 556.9 |
| `ac3db731b3` (#45917) | 217.2 / 212.7 / 217.4 | 215.8 | 4.43 ms | 550.2 / 551.0 / 536.9 | 546.0 |
| `ac3db731b3` + this PR | 228.4 / 228.2 / 229.1 | **228.5** | 4.21 ms | 556.1 / 559.5 / 560.7 | **558.8** |
| `main` `9691e711cd` | 216.8 / 213.9 / 216.2 | 215.6 | 4.47 ms | 548.4 / 549.0 / 516.0 | 537.8 |
| `main` `9691e711cd` + this PR | 226.6 / 227.1 / 226.5 | **226.7 (+5.1%)** | 4.24 ms | 552.6 / 555.0 / 554.3 | **554.0** |

A torch-profiler capture of 20 bs=1 decode steps shows that, with this PR, the per-step kernel list matches the parent of #45917: the same kernel count and the same GEMM tactics, with no `_router_triton_kernel` or `mask_topk_ids_padded_region`. The issue has the full repro steps.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing behavior or flag changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Rerun it with /rerun-failed-ci, or dispatch the pr-test-xeon.yml workflow manually.

[by Claude Code] @ch-wan Thanks, agreed. The padding-only fast path must not skip the side effects of `select_experts`. Fixed in 7b6680467d.

**Change**
- `BypassedTopKOutput.needs_select_experts` (`topk.py`) is true when routing straight from logits would skip work that `select_experts` does:
  - the placement remap;
  - routed-expert capture (`allow_routed_experts_capture` with an active capturer);
  - expert-distribution recording (`expert_distribution_recorder_mode` set);
  - routing simulation (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_UNIFORM_EXPERTS` / `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ROUND_ROBIN_EXPERTS`).

  This is the same set `mimo_v2` already uses to gate its bypassed TopK.
- The FP8 TRT-LLM runner materializes whenever `needs_select_experts` is true; a bare padding bound still keeps the in-kernel router. The predicate doesn't depend on the bound, so it also covers the unbounded EP=1 FP8 path you mentioned.
- The tc-piecewise guard in `FusedMoE.forward` uses the same predicate. Without that, EP=1 with capture under tc-piecewise would reach the opaque logits-only op, which rebuilds a partial `TopKConfig`, and then materialize from it.

**Regression tests** (`test_topk_routing_inputs.py`)
- `test_fp8_padding_bound_still_runs_select_experts_hooks`: bound present, no placement remap. Capture, recording and simulation are each enabled in turn. The runner must reach the routed kernel, and the hook must see the real-row IDs.
- `test_piecewise_lazy_routing_with_capture_keeps_the_full_config`: an unbounded lazy output with capture enabled under tc-piecewise must go through `forward_impl`, not the opaque op.
- On the previous head they fail with exactly 4 failures (capture, recording and simulation subtests, plus the piecewise test). With this commit they pass.

**Validation on 1x GB200** (`lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`)
- **Unit tests** (11 files: `test_topk_routing_inputs`, `test_flashinfer_dispatcher`, `test_standard_dispatcher`, `test_standard_dispatcher_runner_backend`, `test_fp8_moe_runner_ownership`, `test_modelopt_nvfp4_moe_dispatch`, `test_mxfp4_sm100_trtllm_gen`, `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer`, `test_deepseek_mla_dispatch`, `test_native_moe_routing_policy`, `test_runtime_context`): 307 passed, 379 subtests passed.
- **`test_flashinfer_fp8_routed.py`:** 2 passed, 12 subtests passed.
- **End to end, your scenario:** `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--tp 4 --ep 4`, auto `flashinfer_trtllm`, a2a `none`, `--enable-return-routed-experts`, no EPLB. `/generate` with `return_routed_experts`, temperature 0, giving 34 tokens x 48 layers x top-10 IDs:

  | Source | Returned IDs | Rows with 10 distinct IDs | SHA-1 |
  | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
  | `main` `5008726431` | valid, 0..511, all 512 experts seen | 100% | `acb9b308836d894e` |
  | previous head of this PR | all zeros | 0% | `ae4081ce70ff5cf0` |
  | this commit | valid, 0..511, all 512 experts seen | 100% | `acb9b308836d894e` (identical to `main`) |

- **Performance, no hooks enabled:** con1 ISL 8000 / OSL 1000 is 226.3 / 227.1 / 221.1 tok/s. Earlier on the same setup, this PR measured 226.7 and `main` 215.6. The fast path is unchanged.

The FP4 and BF16 TRT-LLM runners never materialized for these hooks, so this PR doesn't regress them, but they still have the unbounded gap. With the shared predicate, fixing them is a one-line follow-up; I can add it here if you'd like.
